subject: Enclave commissioning kickoff & network specs clarifications
messages:
From: Katie Moss <katie.moss@greenbridge.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Greenbridge NetOps <netops@greenbridge.io>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commissioning kickoff & quick checklist

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to get the Private deployment standing up in our staging VPC. We’d like to run a short commissioning kickoff to align network handoff, service accounts, and the environment validation steps.

Questions we have up front so the meeting is productive:
- Which port ranges need to be open egress/ingress to support the Redwood runtime (master/agent/etc)?
- Do you require dedicated service accounts per environment, or will a single shared service principal suffice for staging?
- How do you expect us to provision KV keys / KMS access for the customer-managed key option?

I attached a basic network diagram showing our current staging VPC and the peering proposal (greenbridge_net_diagram.pdf). Can we do a 30-minute kickoff today at 11am PT? If not, tomorrow morning works as well.

Appreciate it —
Katie Moss
Senior PM, Integrations
Greenbridge Health

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Katie Moss <katie.moss@greenbridge.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commissioning kickoff & quick checklist

Katie — thanks for the diagram and the clear questions. 11am PT today works for our infra lead (Ben). Quick answers up front, and I’ll bring a short checklist to the call: 

- Ports: we need egress to the Redwood control plane on TCP 443 and outbound connectivity for model pulls to model storage (range will depend on your registry; we can narrow during call). Inbound is minimal — only our agent health endpoint if you want to NAT it; otherwise we operate outbound-only.
- Service accounts: strongly recommended to use dedicated service accounts per environment (staging/prod) for auditability. We can accept a single cross-environment principal temporarily but will require rotation and scoped roles.
- KMS: for customer-managed keys we ask for a service account with Encrypt/Decrypt and Get/WrapKey permissions; we’ll provide the exact IAM policy.

I’ve pasted an Environment Commissioning Checklist below (short-form) — we’ll walk through and mark ownership on the call.

ENVIRONMENT COMMISSIONING CHECKLIST (short)
- Account & billing contact confirmed
- VPC CIDR & subnet mapping to match Redwood agent sizing
- Route table and NAT for agent outbound connectivity
- Firewall egress rules for control plane (443) and storage registry
- Service accounts created with least privilege roles
- KMS key provisioned (if CSEK requested) + access test
- DNS entries for internal services (if required)
- Logs & metrics collection destination (customer-owned or Redwoods proxy)
- Validation plan: smoke requests, KV cache warmup, load spike test

Attachments: redwood_vpc_prereqs.md (short prio checklist), sow-greenbridge-draft.pdf (SOW draft)

See you at 11 — joining info: Zoom link (sent separately).

—Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Katie Moss <katie.moss@greenbridge.io>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commissioning kickoff & quick checklist

Bringing some infra specifics so NetOps can validate config quickly:

- Egress endpoints: control-plane.redwood.ai:443 and model-storage.redwood.ai:443. If you need IP ranges, we can provide the signed list; but prefer DNS-based egress rules to support IP churn.
- NAT: agents must be able to maintain long-lived outbound connections for KV cache keepalives. NAT timeouts should be >= 10 minutes or enable TCP keepalive.
- MTU: set to 9001 on the peering interfaces if you plan to support jumbo frames — agents can send larger model segments. Not required but helps throughput.
- BGP/Peering: we do not require BGP; VPC peering or a private link is fine. If using transit, ensure route propagation is enabled.
- Ports: aside from 443 egress, allow outbound 53 (DNS) and 123 (NTP) for accurate timestamps in logs.

I’ll share a slim config snippet after the call and a scoped IAM role that only allows object reads from the model registry.

—Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Greenbridge NetOps <netops@greenbridge.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Katie Moss <katie.moss@greenbridge.io>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commissioning kickoff & quick checklist

Thanks for the call yesterday — helpful. Couple clarifications from our side after review of the diagram: 

- We prefer explicit IP ranges for our firewall policy (change window/regulatory control). Can you provide a signed list of egress IPs for the control-plane and storage endpoints? If not, can you provide a predictable hostname rotation schedule?
- For KMS, our security team wants to ensure the key lifecycle meets our compliance policy. Can you confirm whether Redwood will need the Decrypt permission on the key or whether we can wrap keys and hand over wrapped keys?
- Service account: we will create one per environment. Please send the minimal IAM role JSON so we can attach it to the account.

Attached: greenbridge_net_diagram.pdf (updated annot), and a readiness worksheet we filled out (we referenced your redwood_vpc_prereqs.md).

Regards,
NetOps Team
Greenbridge Health
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Greenbridge NetOps <netops@greenbridge.io>, Katie Moss <katie.moss@greenbridge.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commissioning kickoff & quick checklist

Great questions — answering succinctly and listing next steps so we have clear owners: 

1) Egress IPs: we maintain a signed, rotating egress IP set. I’ve attached the first export (greenbridge_net_diagram.pdf annotated) and will put the published IP list into the Drive folder (related link). For firewall windows, using DNS-based rules is acceptable if you can accept the rotation cadence; otherwise we’ll provide a 30-day IP snapshot for policy.

2) KMS model: Redwood prefers the customer to retain control. Two supported flows: 
- Customer-managed key (we request Decrypt for runtime via a scoped service account), or
- Wrapped key flow where you produce wrapped model keys and we never see raw key material (requires additional handshake).
We can share implementation notes for both; please tell us which your security team prefers.

3) IAM role JSON & minimal scope: attached as redwood_vpc_prereqs.md (bottom section) and I’ll sync with Ben to extract the exact policy JSON.

Next steps (owners):
- Greenbridge NetOps: confirm whether you prefer DNS-based egress rules or IP snapshots (by EOD Fri)
- Greenbridge Sec: choose KMS flow (by Tue 08/10)
- Redwood (Ben): produce minimal IAM role JSON + egress IP snapshot (if requested)
- Redwood (Kimberly): finalize SOW draft and circulate DocuSign link (I sent the draft; will update after policy decisions)

Attachments: sow-greenbridge-draft.pdf, redwood_vpc_prereqs.md, greenbridge_net_diagram.pdf

Thanks — we’ll treat the policy choices as blockers for production; staging can proceed under scoped exceptions.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
